source.title: Family Therapy: Concepts and Methods
source.notReproduced: Book prose, figures, case histories, and clinical tools are not republished.

method.scope: Reviewed and mapped mechanisms and contextual cautions across the Introduction and all 15 substantive chapters (printed pp. 1–257). Also inspected the glossary, reference section and index for terminology; they are not separate relational patterns.
method.preciseLimit: Whole-volume concept inventory, source-section review and page-specific mapping; not a certified sentence-by-sentence verification or independent evaluation of every cited primary study.
method.whatIsExpert: The named family-therapy constructs and cautions come from the supplied edition. Page references locate the relevant discussion.
method.whatIsEditorial: All learned expectations, protective responses, reality-check questions, suggested revised expectations, fictional evidence statements, examples, taxonomy and relationship-safety applications are original Clearframe formulations.
method.notSupported: The ledger does not show that Clearframe detects abuse, motives, clinical diagnoses or causal childhood origins. Source clinical effectiveness data concern therapies, not this app.
method.safety: Violence, physical threats or confinement cannot be cancelled by friendly observations elsewhere. Mutual influence does not imply equal responsibility.
method.persona: An imposed interpretation, consequence or compulsory role is the mechanism; immutable characteristics, personality descriptions and cultural identity are not symptoms.

observations.summary: A classic double-bind interpretation requires repeated contradictory injunctions, an important bond and blocked response or escape.
observations.rationale: A single confusing statement does not establish this historical construct.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Pseudomutuality, pseudohostility, outsider fences and mystification describe distinguishable interaction questions.
observations.rationale: Practical observable consequences are mapped without claiming original illness hypotheses.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Postmodern and feminist critiques question professional power to define a single ideal family.
observations.rationale: Model labels must remain revisable and cannot assign pathology from identity or composition.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Positive and negative feedback are technical amplification and correction, not judgments of moral goodness.
observations.rationale: Avoid labeling every stabilizing response as malign or every change as beneficial.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Morphogenesis, open systems and equifinality allow adaptation and different paths to similar outcomes.
observations.rationale: Conceptual models, not individual control behavior.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Child attachment research does not automatically prove the childhood cause of adult relational conduct.
observations.rationale: Do not diagnose attachment style or attribute a motive from an app report.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Questions about who participates, what happened, and why now help correct an initial referral account.
observations.rationale: Clinician interview questions; not a separate control mechanism.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Conjoint approaches may be inappropriate when ongoing coercion or serious violence creates risk.
observations.rationale: The app cannot authorize couples treatment or infer that partners are equally responsible.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Privacy, dual relationships, value imposition, competence and informed consent constrain professional action.
observations.rationale: Principles guide institutional pattern entries; specific legal duties vary by place and time.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Bowen’s projected anxiety and multigenerational scripts are useful exploratory hypotheses, not established causes of disease.
observations.rationale: Do not convert a historical therapeutic formulation into a deterministic verdict.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Genograms and relationship-process questions can organize accounts across generations.
observations.rationale: Recording family facts does not by itself verify causal conclusions.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Metacommunication, reframing and strategic direction can alter how a problem is approached.
observations.rationale: A therapy intervention is not automatically an example of an authority exerting control.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Paradoxical and hidden strategic directions invite critiques of clinician manipulation and inadequate transparency.
observations.rationale: Assess consent and outcome; do not copy intervention scripts into app advice.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Subsystem membership and boundary permeability vary by household and stage of life.
observations.rationale: Ordinary flexible closeness and separation are not signs of pathology.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Enactment, joining, boundary making and unbalancing are structured clinician actions.
observations.rationale: Not ready-made household control subroutines.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Congruent expression separates felt emotion, communication and consequential action.
observations.rationale: No emotion by itself establishes fault or intent.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Satir-inspired exercises, EFT and parts language explore emotion and relational vulnerability.
observations.rationale: Do not infer unconscious parts or assign compulsory disclosure.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Transference, splitting and projective identification are theoretical explanations, not observable diagnoses.
observations.rationale: Map specific responses and counterexamples without attributing an unobserved unconscious cause.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Psychodynamic case-based evidence and interpretive uncertainty constrain causal claims.
observations.rationale: The app cannot verify why a person feels, acts or recalls in a particular way.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Contingent reinforcement, intermittent reward, aversive cycles and functional assessment describe how responses can be maintained.
observations.rationale: A pattern alone cannot establish deliberate manipulation by another actor.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Specific interpretation errors should be checked with contrary information and perspective reversal.
observations.rationale: Swap Shoes is a prompt, not independent confirmation of the user’s facts.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Sex therapy protocols and treatment-trial results have population, consent and intervention-specific limits.
observations.rationale: Not suitable for generic nonclinical pattern cues.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Agency over choices differs from authority imposed on others, and gendered social arrangements can restrict both.
observations.rationale: Concrete unequal conduct matters; sex and gender do not determine the pattern.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Race, disability, immigration, faith and sexual or gender minority status can affect safety and access to support.
observations.rationale: Avoid pathologizing personal identity or claiming a universal family norm.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Digital context changes rapidly; numerical screen-time claims in an older textbook should not be copied as timeless rules.
observations.rationale: Use actual consent, interference and safety events rather than moralizing usage.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Single-parent, remarried, community and chosen-family contexts can each include both support and real constraints.
observations.rationale: Household composition does not itself create a controlling persona.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Family hostility or accommodation may affect stress and illness course without making relatives the cause of schizophrenia.
observations.rationale: Avoid illness blame and clinical predictions.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Discernment and consent permit repair, separation or nonparticipation depending on safety and individual preference.
observations.rationale: The tool should not make reconciliation a required outcome.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Client-defined small goals and exceptions help test a dominant problem story.
observations.rationale: Useful for reflection; no guarantee that a chosen experiment changes another person.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Case examples and studies of solution-focused treatment have differing strengths and scope.
observations.rationale: Do not transfer treatment outcome claims to this application.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Externalization, unique outcomes, re-authoring and outsider witnesses support preferred meaning.
observations.rationale: Metaphorical language cannot absolve the actor of an actual threat.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Supportive narrative reframing can still ignore physical power, material limits or valid anger.
observations.rationale: Check behavior and context separately from preferred stories.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Family theories focus on different units and evidence types: individual history, two-person cycles, alliances, and social barriers.
observations.rationale: None is a privileged complete explanation for every incident.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Acceptance is appropriate for nonharmful differences; severe coercion still calls for protection and accountability.
observations.rationale: Do not turn encouragement to accept preferences into tolerance for abuse.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Efficacy, real-world effectiveness, researcher allegiance and sampling all affect conclusions.
observations.rationale: A cited positive study does not validate a Clearframe indicator as a diagnostic measure.

observations.attribution: Nichols and Davis (including named schools or cited studies as indicated in the textbook)
observations.summary: Chosen goals, acceptable methods, rapport and extratherapeutic resources influence treatment.
observations.rationale: Progress cannot be attributed solely to personal effort or a credential.
